request.prompt: Which humanoid robots can be purchased in North America?

result.text:
Purchasing a humanoid robot in North America generally falls into two distinct categories: readily available developer/research platforms that can be ordered directly online, and industrial/commercial enterprise models that require direct corporate requests-for-quote (RFQs), pilot programs, or Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) agreements.

1. Developer & Research Models (Available via E-Commerce)

These units can be bought directly through global manufacturers or North American robotics distributors like RobotShop Professional Humanoid Robots Catalog:

Unitree G1 — An ultra-compact developer and research bipedal humanoid with 23 degrees of freedom. It is available in base configurations or upgraded EDU variants.

Estimated Price: Starts around $17,900 for the base model; EDU and Ultimate research configurations range from $43,900 to over $83,000.
Where to buy: Available on the Unitree G1 Collection on RobotShop or direct from Unitree.

Unitree R1 / R1 EDU — A versatile lower-cost humanoid/bipedal developer platform.

Estimated Price: Starts around $8,990 up to $32,900 for advanced EDU Pro variants.
Where to buy: RobotShop Professional Humanoid Robots Catalog.

Booster Robotics K1 Series — Educational and professional humanoid systems designed for research, AI training, and classroom interaction.

Estimated Price: Roughly $11,800 to $20,200 depending on the GEEK, Educational, or Professional tier.
Where to buy: RobotShop Professional Humanoid Robots Catalog.

2. Industrial & Commercial Enterprise Models (By Quote / Pilot Only)

If you are looking for full-sized deployment humanoids meant for logistics, manufacturing, or general labor, direct e-commerce checkout is not available. Enterprises must engage in corporate sales pipelines, volume allocations, or RaaS lease models:

Agility Robotics Digit — Designed specifically for logistics, warehouse tote handling, and cross-docking. Deployed via multi-unit commercial pilots (such as with Amazon).

Estimated Price: Circulates around $250,000 per unit or via RaaS deployment structures.
Ordering Pathway: Direct corporate RFQ through Agility Robotics.

Sanctuary AI Phoenix — A high-dexterity general-purpose humanoid powered by their Carbon AI platform, targeted at retail and light manufacturing.

Estimated Price: Estimated between $150,000 and $300,000 under structured enterprise pilot agreements.
Ordering Pathway: Enterprise pilot application via Sanctuary AI.

Apptronik Apollo & Figure Series (e.g., Figure 03) — Advanced general-purpose commercial humanoids scaling up factory and warehouse integrations.

Estimated Price: Quote-only / unreleased public retail price.
Ordering Pathway: Enterprise allocation requests through Apptronik or Figure AI.

Tesla Optimus — Targeted at high-volume industrial scaling and eventual consumer use, though wider market availability remains constrained to internal manufacturing priorities and future waitlists.

If you are looking to purchase one, tell me:

Are you buying for academic research/development or industrial automation/business operations?
What is your budget range?

I can help narrow down the ideal platform and connect you with the right procurement channel.
